source.title: LR-0002: CHIP-8 Codebase Audit & Architecture Baseline

cards.question: What core architectural modules compose the composite Chip8 state struct in a modular C emulator?
cards.answer: Memory (4KB RAM), Registers (16 general-purpose, I, PC, timers), Stack (16-level call stack and SP), Screen (64x32 monochrome display), and Keyboard (16-key keypad state).

cards.question: Why should emulator structs be passed via pointers (e.g. chip8_init(Chip8 *chip8)) rather than by value in C?
cards.answer: Passing by value copies the entire struct (including the 4KB RAM buffer and screen matrix) onto the stack on every call, causing severe performance degradation and stack pressure.

cards.question: Why is modular separation into dedicated translation units (memory.c, screen.c, registers.c) preferred in C17?
cards.answer: It enforces encapsulation via header contracts, enables independent compilation, and isolates memory access logic to dedicated modules.
